issues: The wordmark was only 132px, reading like a small headline in a 1920-wide frame with empty space everywhere, with none of the weight a brand's first beat needs
The background was a flat off-white with nothing but the text, so no paused frame looked like a designed poster
The mono kicker was pale and tightly tracked, reading like placeholder text, and the brand name was a long real-institution-style name
The press was just scale plus blur with no sense of dropping from the air into paper, and the amber glint dash was too thin to see
changes: Sand look (cotton paper, ink, terracotta); the stage is now a letterpress proof sheet with corner crop marks, side registration marks, a colour bar and proof number as a dimmed texture layer
The wordmark is the fictional brand 'Kestrel.' in a 280px bold serif spanning ~55% of the width; the terracotta period is the only accent, landing last and pressing hardest
The press has height: each letter hangs at 1.45x with a cast shadow that tightens as it falls, slams in with ease-in, then squashes slightly with an 8f ink spread
The glint became a terracotta rule that extends segment by segment under each landing letter with a bright head, the shot's single highlight, which then stays as the lockup divider
Retimed to 120f: crosshair and crop marks draw from frame 0, press 18-53, typing 54-74, a 51f hold with a 1.2% slow push, then a 10f ease-in rise-and-defocus exit
The kicker is now 34px wide-tracked mono 'RESEARCH CONSOLE FOR TEAMS' with a terracotta block cursor, contrasting serif against mono
